coachingPoints: Land truly simultaneous on both feet — a staggered landing is a travel risk.
Keep the hop short; a long hop carries you into the defender instead of stopping before them.
Ball stays high during the hop — low gathers invite strips.
Use a shot fake after landing only if the defender stays grounded; otherwise just go up.
Bend your knees on landing so you can explode up immediately.
commonMistakes: Hopping too far and landing under the basket — now you're stuck with no angle.
Landing one foot before the other — referees call this a travel at higher levels.
Dropping the ball low after the hop — defenders strip it; keep it at chin level.
Not stopping at all — a fake hop that doesn't change speed fools nobody.
description: A small two-foot jump that stops your drive on a dime, beats the shot blocker, and sets up a balanced finish.
gameSituations: Drives where the shot blocker rotates late — stop before them and finish as they fly by.
Transition 2-on-1 when the defender commits to the ball — hop, then finish or dish.
Against aggressive closeouts — pro hop off the catch sets up a clean pull-up too.

howTo.detail: Attack the paint at pace. As you approach the restricted area, gather the ball with two hands, ready to pick up your dribble.
howTo.title: Drive with a gather in mind

howTo.detail: Take a short hop forward — 30 to 60 cm — and land on both feet at the same time, knees bent, in a jump-stop position. This is the entire move; keep it compact.
howTo.title: Small hop, two-foot landing

howTo.detail: Hold the ball at chest or chin height with a shot fake or eyes up. The defender, already committed to your drive, will jump or lean past you.
howTo.title: Freeze the defender

howTo.detail: As the defender leaves your space, explode straight up off both feet and finish softly. Because you stopped in balance, your shot has normal form and soft touch.
howTo.title: Rise in balance

title: Pro Hop
whatIsIt: The pro hop is a short, controlled two-foot jump used to stop a drive suddenly, usually right in front of a shot blocker or help defender. You hop, land on two feet simultaneously, and rise into a balanced finish — all while the defender flies past.

It is the deceleration counter to the euro step's lateral move. Where the euro dodges sideways, the pro hop stops time: defenders committed to contesting a full-speed drive end up out of position while you're landing in perfect balance.
whyItMatters: Most defenders time their jump to your drive's rhythm. A sudden two-foot stop breaks that timing completely and turns a contested drive into an open, balanced shot. It also draws fouls, because late-arriving defenders land on you.
